drhp.business: Merritronix is a B2B ESDM company specializing in high-reliability, mission-critical electronic assemblies and systems for defence, aerospace, telecommunications and specialized industrial electronics. Its integrated offering spans component sourcing, PCB (SMT/THT) assembly, system integration, testing and box-build/finished-product delivery, executed to defence and aerospace quality standards. Revenue is derived from turnkey manufacturing/build-to-print, obsolescence engineering management, trading sales and job work.

drhp.expansion: The Company intends to deploy IPO net proceeds towards capital expenditure on machinery and equipment (up to Rs. 2,136.43 lakhs, planned for FY2026-27) to expand its Hyderabad manufacturing capacity. Its installed capacity as on March 31, 2026 was 10,75,000 boards p.a. for SMT, 6,00,000 boards p.a. for THT and 4,20,000 units p.a. for box build, aggregating 17,85,000 production units per annum. Growth is being driven by increased order volumes from defence and aerospace customers, capacity expansion and a progressive shift toward higher-value turnkey manufacturing.
drhp.mdna: Revenue mix shift toward the higher-margin Aerospace & Defence segment (52.94% of revenue in FY2023 to 88.50% in FY2025)|Operating leverage as a relatively stable fixed/semi-fixed cost base (employee, finance, depreciation, admin) was absorbed over a larger revenue base|Growth in turnkey projects and complex defence assemblies commanding higher value addition versus standalone component supply|Strong repeat-customer base contributing approximately 80% to 94% of total customers, aiding revenue visibility|Execution of larger and higher-value orders; improved profitability lowering debt-equity …

products.note: Lifecycle extension for legacy defence/aerospace electronic platforms (avionics, naval, surveillance, ground-based communication) whose components are no longer manufactured

Procurement from authorized global suppliers and direct sale to customers; pre-emptive stocking of long-lead/supply-constrained parts. Sale of telecom cable jointing kits was undertaken in the past and has since been discontinued

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Integrated in-house B2B ESDM model spanning component sourcing, PCB assembly (SMT and through-hole), system integration, functional/reliability testing, quality assurance, box-build and delivery of finished electronic products under a single coordinated customer interface, providing end-to-end component traceability. Mechanical enclosure fabrication and related processes are outsourced to third-party vendors where required. Components are procured from a network of authorized global suppliers, with long-lead or supply-constrained critical parts pre-emptively stocked (trading sales segment) to mitigate supply-chain risk and reduce lead times. The Company states a strategic progression up the value chain toward higher-complexity turnkey and obsolescence-management engagements and intends to strengthen system-level design and participate in Joint Manufacturing Models (JMM).

genesis.founding_story: Incorporated on October 14, 1988 as 'Merritronix Private Limited' under the Companies Act, 1956 pursuant to a certificate of incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies, Andhra Pradesh. financial_valuation.detail: Cash flows from operating activities negative in FY26 and FY25 driven by working-capital build-up (inventory and WIP) amid ~34% revenue CAGR; company frames it as timing/scaling, not profitability, issue.

financial_valuation.title: Negative operating cash flows in prior periods

internal_operational.detail: Company generally does not obtain firm long-term purchase commitments; arrangements have no minimum-order, take-or-pay or binding volume guarantees and no termination/exit/unilateral withdrawal clauses. Cancellations, reductions or delays could harm operating results and working capital.
internal_operational.title: No long-term customer commitments; orders may be cancelled, changed or delayed

internal_operational.detail: Assembles complex customized PCBs for mission-critical defence/aerospace applications; failure to meet specifications (EN 9100:2018 / AS 9100D / ISO 9001:2015) can trigger recalls, warranty claims, order cancellations and reputational damage.
internal_operational.evidence: Five areas for improvement identified in certification audits over last three FYs; all classified Minor, 100% closed; zero repeated non-conformities over three-year cycle
internal_operational.title: Strict quality requirements, customer inspections and audits

internal_operational.detail: Sources PCBs, passive/semiconductor components, ICs, microcontrollers, FPGAs, DSPs, RF power amplifiers, CPLDs, connectors from domestic and foreign suppliers; no firm long-term pricing arrangements; may be unable to pass on cost escalation.
internal_operational.title: Increases in raw material prices

strategy_growth.detail: Operates predominantly as a B2B ESDM contract manufacturer without a consumer-facing brand; dependent on purchase orders, program awards and renewals from a concentrated defence/industrial customer base; typically does not own product IP; limited brand visibility may constrain pricing power, customer diversification and growth.
strategy_growth.evidence: Certifications EN 9100:2018, IPC-A-610 Class 3; AOI, X-ray, functional testing; no direct exposure to government defence spending but indirect via customers
strategy_growth.title: B2B ESDM model with limited brand recognition

strategy_growth.detail: Growth depends on qualifying for and winning competitive bids from Defence PSUs based on pricing, technical expertise, reputation, financing and track record; pre-qualification criteria may evolve; increased competition could reduce market share.
strategy_growth.evidence: Significant portion of business obtained through competitive bidding and pre-qualification processes
strategy_growth.title: May not qualify for or win future bids

strategy_growth.detail: Highly competitive ESDM industry with pressure on pricing and market share; competes with independent suppliers, distributors and OEM in-house operations, plus larger competitors and firms in China and Vietnam benefiting from economies of scale.
strategy_growth.evidence: Competes on product quality, technology, cost, delivery and service; expects competition from ESDM companies in China and Vietnam
strategy_growth.title: Increasing competition in the ESDM industry

concerns_observed: Severe customer concentration: top-1 customer 62.08%, top-5 80.11% and top-10 89.36% of FY26 revenue; loss of a single large client would be material.

Operating cash flow was negative in FY26 (Rs -2,338.21 lakhs) and FY25 (Rs -664.33 lakhs), driven by inventory build-up (inventory Rs 3,349.77 to Rs 7,130.76 lakhs; inventory days 92 to 130) and receivables growth (Rs 1,118.73 to Rs 3,654.65 lakhs); reported earnings are not yet converting to cash.

Rising leverage: total debt grew from Rs 1,581.78 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 4,319.74 lakhs (FY26) with secured borrowings at 94.12% of indebtedness; total working capital requirement rose to Rs 6,532.88 lakhs (Mar 2026).

Concentration in Aerospace & Defence at 97.81% of FY26 revenue (up from 80.26% in FY24), Turnkey/build-to-print at 92.07%, and Telangana geography at 98.19% - limited diversification across end-industry, product and region.

100% of the estimated Rs 2,136.43 lakhs machinery/equipment capex remains un-ordered as of the RHP date; orders rest on third-party quotations, and nearly all listed machinery is sourced from a single supplier (Maxim SMT Technologies Pvt. Ltd.), with the Objects not appraised by any bank or financial institution.

Extensive related-party dependence: registered office and plant leased from related party Amar Electronics on stated below-market, non-arm's-length rent (lease to 31/03/2030); purchases from promoter proprietorship Sunrise Telecom of Rs 228.80 lakhs (FY26); large short-term advances to promoter Dovari Amarnath (Rs 554.77 lakhs given FY25, Rs 480.62 lakhs FY24).
RoNW declined from 53.34% (FY25) to 30.66% (FY26) as the equity base expanded via bonus and preferential issues, so headline return ratios are diluting even as absolute profit grows.
Bonus issue (13:2) on May 23, 2025 falls within 18 months of the proposed issue; multiple preferential issues (Sep 2025, Dec 2025, Mar 2026 at Rs 108.40) occurred shortly before the IPO.

parameter_scores.basis: Revenue Rs 8,569.91 to Rs 11,356.38 to Rs 15,589.56 lakhs FY24-FY26 (~35% CAGR); order book Rs 9,664.91 lakhs as of April 30, 2026 and 86.08% repeat-customer rate support near-term visibility.

EBITDA margin expanded 7.82% to 17.42% and PAT margin 3.56% to 10.33% FY24-FY26; PAT Rs 305.03 to Rs 1,610.30 lakhs. Tempered by sustainability questions given the rising A&D/turnkey mix and no long-term pricing arrangements.

Negative CFO in FY26 (Rs -2,338.21 lakhs) and FY25 (Rs -664.33 lakhs); inventory days rose to 130; total debt up to Rs 4,319.74 lakhs (secured 94.12%); working capital need Rs 6,532.88 lakhs. Cushioned by cash of Rs 2,569.62 lakhs and networth Rs 5,312.96 lakhs at FY26.
Top-1 customer 62.08%, top-5 80.11%, top-10 89.36% of FY26 revenue; supplier top-10 at 90.74% (per risk disclosure); Aerospace & Defence 97.81% and Telangana 98.19% of FY26 revenue.

Below-market non-arm's-length lease from Amar Electronics; purchases from promoter concern Sunrise Telecom (Rs 228.80 lakhs FY26); large promoter advances (Rs 554.77 lakhs FY25); Section 185 compounding fee Rs 5,00,000; directors linked to 5 struck-off companies and a prior (vacated) Section 164 disqualification; executive directors lack listed-company experience; untraceable historical records.

100% of Rs 2,136.43 lakhs machinery capex un-ordered at RHP date, sourced almost entirely from one supplier (Maxim SMT); Objects not bank-appraised; Rs 1,271.92 lakhs of proceeds toward debt repayment creates no tangible assets; entire deployment planned within FY2026-27.

Promoter holding 85.17% pre-issue (post-issue not stated); no OFS; no pledging. Offset by a 13:2 bonus within 18 months, three pre-IPO preferential issues, and promoter average acquisition cost of Rs 0.78-1.26 versus the proposed issue price.

red_flags: Operating cash flow negative for two consecutive years (FY25 and FY26) despite rising reported profits, indicating earnings are absorbed by working-capital growth.
Extreme single-customer dependence (top-1 at 62.08% of FY26 revenue) with no long-term or take-or-pay commitments disclosed.
Registered office and manufacturing facility leased from related party Amar Electronics on an explicitly non-arm's-length, below-market-rent basis.
Large short-term advances to promoter Dovari Amarnath (Rs 554.77 lakhs in FY25) and a Rs 5,00,000 Section 185 compounding fee, indicating past promoter-financing and compliance issues.
Directors associated with five ROC struck-off companies plus a prior (since-vacated) Section 164(2) disqualification.
100% of Rs 2,136.43 lakhs machinery capex un-ordered at RHP date, with Objects not appraised by any bank or financial institution.
Untraceable historical corporate records (company incorporated 1988) and a director appointment-date discrepancy, with reliance on a PCS search report.
strengths_observed: Revenue scaled from Rs 8,569.91 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 11,356.38 lakhs (FY25) to Rs 15,589.56 lakhs (FY26), roughly 35% CAGR over two years.

PAT rose from Rs 305.03 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 865.95 lakhs (FY25) to Rs 1,610.30 lakhs (FY26), with PAT margin expanding 3.56% to 7.63% to 10.33% and EBITDA margin 7.82% to 13.31% to 17.42%; EPS 2.80 to 7.95 to 13.92.
Consistently high return ratios: ROCE 43.13% to 66.21% to 45.26% and ROE 44.22% to 69.21% to 46.03% across FY24-FY26.

Disclosed order book of Rs 9,664.91 lakhs as of April 30, 2026 (aggregate order value Rs 13,833.95 lakhs, of which Rs 4,169.04 lakhs completed) across 15 clients, with an 86.08% repeat-customer rate (68 of 79 active customers) for the period ended March 31, 2026.
EN 9100:2018 (AS 9100D / ISO 9001:2015 equivalent) and IPC-A-610 Class 3 qualification supporting defence/aerospace PCBA work; high utilisation on TMD (99.00%) and Box Build (98.93%) lines in FY26.
No Offer for Sale; entire issue is a fresh issue of up to 47,00,000 shares, so proceeds accrue to the company. Promoters report no pledged or encumbered shares.
Networth strengthened from Rs 818.20 lakhs (FY24) to Rs 5,312.96 lakhs (FY26), aided by preferential issues, expanding the equity base ahead of listing.

summary.oneLiner: A high-reliability, mission-critical electronics systems design and manufacturing (ESDM) company serving India's strategic defence and aerospace programmes.
summary.business: Merritronix is a B2B ESDM company specializing in high-reliability, mission-critical electronic assemblies and systems for defence, aerospace, telecommunications and specialized industrial electronics. Its integrated offering spans component sourcing, PCB (SMT/THT) assembly, system integration, testing and box-build/finished-product delivery, executed to defence and aerospace quality standards. Revenue is derived from turnkey manufacturing/build-to-print, obsolescence engineering management, trading sales and job work.

certifications.body:

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Integrated in-house B2B ESDM model spanning component sourcing, PCB assembly (SMT and through-hole), system integration, functional/reliability testing, quality assurance, box-build and delivery of finished electronic products under a single coordinated customer interface, providing end-to-end component traceability. Mechanical enclosure fabrication and related processes are outsourced to third-party vendors where required. Components are procured from a network of authorized global suppliers, with long-lead or supply-constrained critical parts pre-emptively stocked (trading sales segment) to mitigate supply-chain risk and reduce lead times. The Company states a strategic progression up the value chain toward higher-complexity turnkey and obsolescence-management engagements and intends to strengthen system-level design and participate in Joint Manufacturing Models (JMM).

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shift toward the higher-margin Aerospace & Defence segment (52.94% of revenue in FY2023 to 88.50% in FY2025)
- Operating leverage as a relatively stable fixed/semi-fixed cost base (employee, finance, depreciation, admin) was absorbed over a larger revenue base
- Growth in turnkey projects and complex defence assemblies commanding higher value addition versus standalone component supply
- Strong repeat-customer base contributing approximately 80% to 94% of total customers, aiding revenue visibility
- Execution of larger and higher-value orders; improved profitability lowering debt-equity …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company intends to deploy IPO net proceeds towards capital expenditure on machinery and equipment (up to Rs. 2,136.43 lakhs, planned for FY2026-27) to expand its Hyderabad manufacturing capacity. Its installed capacity as on March 31, 2026 was 10,75,000 boards p.a. for SMT, 6,00,000 boards p.a. for THT and 4,20,000 units p.a. for box build, aggregating 17,85,000 production units per annum. Growth is being driven by increased order volumes from defence and aerospace customers, capacity expansion and a progressive shift toward higher-value turnkey manufacturing.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Three decades of operating legacy in mission-critical defence and aerospace electronics (low-volume, high-complexity, high-reliability niche)
- High entry barriers: EN 9100:2018 (AS 9100D) certification, IPC-A-610 Class 3 qualification and mission-critical delivery track record typically take 18-24 months to obtain
- Integrated execution framework unifying sourcing, assembly, testing and quality control, supporting component traceability required in defence/aerospace
- Established track record delivering imaging infrared seeker assemblies for missile systems, electronic assemblies for airborne …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- May restrict pricing power, customer diversification and growth; Company does not own the IP in products it manufactures and has limited control over specifications, pricing and product life cycles
- Revenues are substantially derived from a concentrated customer base and dependent on purchase orders, programme awards and contract renewals rather than diversified end-consumer demand
- Aerospace & defence applications accounted for 97.81% of FY2026 revenue, exposing the Company to defence budget/programme cycles
- Telangana contributed 98.19% of revenue in FY2026, concentrating operational and demand risk
- Any reduction, delay, modification or cancellation of purchase orders or programme awards could adversely affect operations
- Company relies heavily on long-tenured promoter-directors (Mr. Dovari Amarnath and Mr. Dovari Yesudas) for technical and strategic leadership

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Deploy IPO net proceeds of up to Rs. 2,136.43 lakhs on capital expenditure for purchase of machinery and equipment, to be utilised in FY2026-27.**
- **Fund working capital requirements with up to Rs. 2,195.21 lakhs of IPO net proceeds in FY2026-27.**
- **Repay/prepay, in full or part, outstanding borrowings using up to Rs. 1,271.92 lakhs of IPO net proceeds in FY2026-27.**
- **Continue a deliberate strategic progression up the electronics manufacturing value chain toward higher-complexity, higher-value programme engagements.**
- **Scale a dedicated obsolescence management capability to serve the growing legacy-platform lifecycle demand across the Indian armed forces and defence PSU supply chain.**
- **Expand Hyderabad manufacturing capacity beyond the 17,85,000 production-unit-per-annum installed base via machinery capex funded by the IPO.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deliberate strategic progression up the electronics manufacturing value chain toward higher-complexity, higher-value programme engagements
- Shift business mix toward higher-margin turnkey manufacturing/build-to-print engagements
- Position as a specialist obsolescence-management provider to the Indian armed forces and defence PSU supply chain
- Capacity expansion funded via IPO capex on machinery and equipment
